concepts.learning_objective: Describe the setting of Lencho's house and explain why he was waiting eagerly for rain.
Interpret Lencho's comparison of raindrops to new coins and what it shows about his hopes.

topics.title: The hailstorm destroys the crop
topics.ncert_sections: The hailstorm and the sorrowful night

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the rain turned into a hailstorm and describe the damage it caused.
Explain the conflict between humans and nature, and between humans themselves, in the story.

topics.title: Lencho's faith and his letter to God
topics.ncert_sections: Lencho writes and posts his letter

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the lines that show Lencho's complete faith in God.
Recall what Lencho asked for in his letter to God and why.

topics.title: The postmaster's act of goodwill
topics.ncert_sections: The post office reads and answers the letter

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the postmaster answered the letter and signed it 'God'.
Recall how the postmaster gathered money for Lencho and how much he could send.

topics.title: Lencho's reply and the irony of the story
topics.ncert_sections: Lencho receives the money and writes again

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the irony in Lencho blaming the post office employees for the missing money.
Evaluate Lencho's character using evidence from the story.

topics.title: Grammar: relative clauses, negatives for emphasis and 'hope'

concepts.learning_objective: Identify non-defining relative clauses and join sentences using who, whom, whose and which.
Distinguish negatives that show absence from negatives used for emphasis.
Distinguish the uses of 'hope' as a noun and as a verb.

topics.title: Metaphors and storm vocabulary
topics.ncert_sections: Thinking about Language I and V

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the metaphors in the story and the qualities they compare.
Match names of storms such as hailstorm, tornado and gale with their descriptions.
